hints: The list is already sorted. If the smallest and largest prices together are too big, which one can never be part of the answer?
Use two pointers from both ends. Compare the sum to target: too small means move the left pointer right, too big means move the right pointer left.

1. Put i at the first index and j at the last.
  2. While i < j, compute s = nums[i] + nums[j].
  3. If s == target, return [i+1, j+1].
  4. If s < target, move i right; otherwise move j left.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Try every pair (i, j) with two nested loops and check the sum.

approaches.name: Better
approaches.idea: For each i, binary search for target − nums[i] in the part after i.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Two pointers from both ends, shrinking the range based on whether the sum is too small or too large.

explain: For [1,4,6,10,13] and target 16: 1+13 = 14 is too small, so move left to 4; 4+13 = 17 is too big, so move right to 10; 4+10 = 14 too small, move left to 6; 6+10 = 16, so return [3,4] (1-based). It works because when the sum is too small, the left value cannot pair with anything (every other partner is even smaller), so discarding it is safe; the same logic applies to the right side. Remember the answer is 1-based, not 0-based.
recognize: Sorted input + find a pair with a given sum → two pointers from both ends.
